Live: Pezeshkian set to address UN for the first time since US, Israel launched Iran war

Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly (UNGA) Wednesday in his first speech at the world body since the US and Israel launched the Iran war. His address comes a day after President Donald Trump told the UNGA he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" and "drive them into hell". Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

        Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, the official news agency IRNA reported.
The announcement was made by Habibollah Abbasi, director general of public relations at the Iranian president's office, in an interview with IRNA published on Monday.
Abbasi said Pezeshkian will deliver a speech at the UNGA's session and hold meetings with other participating countries' leaders and officials during the trip.
The US government had refrained from issuing visas to some members of the Iranian delegation, including those of the president's media team, he said.
The 81st session of the UNGA opened on September 8, while the general debate will begin from September 22 at UN Headquarters in New York and continue through September 26 and on September 28.
Pezeshkian's planned visit comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the US, with Iranian officials warning of a strong response to any further military action against the country.
Iran will definitely change the "geography" of the war with the United States and Israel if it comes under another "invasion," Hossein Mohebbi, spokesperson of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), has said.
"If another invasion is launched (against Iran), there will be significant changes in our defense and offense ... We will definitely change the war's geography," Mohebbi said in an interview with Iran's Al-Alam news channel published Sunday night.
"We will certainly introduce new weapons with new capabilities into the fray, and the world will be astonished," Mohebbi said. "We have new targets that have not been attacked yet."
Mohebbi emphasized that the war has not ended yet, and the IRGC has prepared itself for a long-term conflict.
Meanwhile, the General Staff of Iran's Armed Forces on Monday vowed "more defeats" for the United States, Israel and their allies.
